Gallbladder surgery is really one of the most common an uninvasive surgeries.

Most animals don't even have a gallbladder, and we humans don't need it either. We can live just as well without.

Added benefit in your case may be, that the gallbladder removal means you have less bile in your body (the gallbladder stores about a full cup of bile), and most people with reflux symptoms do way better after the surgery.

Note: as far as side effects are concerned, there are wide ranges of things that people experience after surgery. I have 3 tiny scares because its an easy surgery and they do not use a single large incision like they previously did. I have know folks to have the acid reflux still after their surgery or even symptoms of IBD (probably GERD). So know that it will not be a miracle sure either.
